mainTopic: The miracles of the שמן המשחה, who is anointed with it and how, and signs for the future
overview: רבי יהודה teaches that the twelve לוג of שמן המשחה made by משה were full of miracles, and that all of it remains for the future, since זה equals twelve. A ברייתא then teaches that a כהן גדול who is the son of a כהן גדול still needs anointing, but a king who is the son of a king does not. A king's son is anointed only when there is a dispute over the throne, as with שלמה, יהואש and יהואחז. The גמרא finds a פסוק for each rule and adds that only kings of בית דוד are anointed. יהוא and יהואחז were anointed with pure balsam, not the holy oil, because the oil had been hidden by יאשיה together with the ארון. Along the way the גמרא sorts out the names and birth order of יאשיהו's sons, and explains that צדקיה was also called שלום and מתניה. It then describes how kings and the כהן גדול are anointed, and tells how the drops of oil on אהרן's beard were not מעילה. The amud ends with the rule that kings are anointed beside a spring, and רב אמי's list of signs about the future, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The oil was full of miracles from beginning to end
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה responds to the concern that twelve לוג was too little. The שמן המשחה had many miracles, not just one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was only one miracle done with the anointing oil? Many miracles were done with it, from beginning to end. At first it was only twelve לוג. Yet it anointed the משכן and its vessels, and אהרן and his sons for all seven ימי המלואים. Later it anointed כהנים גדולים and kings. And all of it is still there for the future.
steps.whatsHappening: Just before this, the גמרא raised a problem: twelve לוג of oil seems far too little for how רבי יהודה says it was made. Here רבי יהודה answers with a question that really means: 'This oil was miraculous anyway, so why be surprised?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not deny that the amount was small. Instead it says the whole history of this oil was a miracle: it was used again and again over the generations and never ran out. So one more miracle in how it was made is no difficulty at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy anointing oil that משה made
A measure of liquid (roughly the volume of six eggs)
The seven days when the משכן and the כהנים were inaugurated

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'was only one miracle done?' is not a real question asking for information. It is a way of answering: since the oil was full of miracles, a miracle in how it was made should not bother us.

steps.terutzMaskana: The oil worked through miracles from start to finish, so its small amount is no problem.

steps.title: Proof from the word זה that the twelve לוג last forever
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק is brought: the word זה equals twelve, which shows the original twelve לוג remain for all generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'This (זה) shall be a holy anointing oil to Me for your generations.' The word זה has the numerical value of twelve. That means the twelve לוג will be there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the last claim, that all the oil still remains for the future. It uses the פסוק and the number value of the word זה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ז is 7 and ה is 5, which makes 12. The פסוק says 'זה will be for your generations', so it is read as 'twelve לוג will be for your generations'. In other words, the same twelve לוג last through every generation.

keyTerms.meaning: The number value of Hebrew letters, used to learn a teaching
They are, they add up to

phrases.english: The word “zeh” (this), in numerical value,

steps.whatToRemember: The original twelve לוג of שמן המשחה were never used up. The word זה (=12) in the פסוק 'for your generations' shows this.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists the miracles of the oil, including what the pot, roots and fire should have used up
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: the oil started as only twelve לוג. A lot should have been lost to the pot, the roots and the fire, yet it still anointed the משכן, its vessels, אהרן and his sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And משה took the anointing oil and anointed the משכן...' רבי יהודה says: the anointing oil that משה made in the desert had many miracles from beginning to end. At first it was only twelve לוג. Think how much the pot soaks up, how much the roots soak up, how much the fire burns! Yet it anointed the משכן and its vessels, and אהרן and his sons all seven ימי המלואים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the same teaching of רבי יהודה in fuller form. It adds details about how the oil should have shrunk while it was being made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is the cooking process. Some oil soaks into the pot, some soaks into the spice roots, and some is burned off by the fire. After all that, almost nothing should have been left, yet it was enough for everything.

keyTerms.meaning: Roots (the spice roots cooked in the oil)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

The anointing oil that Moses made in the wilderness,

how much does a cauldron absorb,

how much does the fire burn up,
and yet with it the Tabernacle and its vessels were anointed,

phrases.aramaic: אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו כָּל שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הַמְּלוּאִים,
phrases.english: and Aaron and his sons, all seven days of the inauguration,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן ״וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A ברייתא version of רבי יהודה's teaching from step 1, with extra detail about how the oil was lost while cooking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שמן המשחה was only twelve לוג. Even after losses to the pot, roots and fire, it miraculously anointed the משכן, its vessels, אהרן and his sons.

steps.title: Who needs anointing: a כהן גדול's son yes, a king's son no
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: כהנים גדולים and kings were anointed with this oil. Even a כהן גדול whose father was a כהן גדול must be anointed, but a king whose father was king is not anointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with it כהנים גדולים and kings were anointed. Even a כהן גדול who is the son of a כהן גדול needs anointing. But we do not anoint a king who is the son of a king.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the list of who used this oil and then adds a new rule: who needs to be anointed and who does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a contrast here. A new כהן גדול always needs anointing, even if his father held the job. A king who inherits the throne from his father is not anointed; the anointing of the father carries over to the son. This rule sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A High Priest who is the son of a High Priest
A king who is the son of a king

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a real rule about כהונה and מלכות. Kingship passes from father to son without a new anointing, but the role of כהן גדול needs a new anointing for each person.

phrases.english: And with it High Priests and kings were anointed.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בֶּן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: And even a High Priest who is the son of a High Priest
requires anointing.
But one does not anoint a king who is the son of a king.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בֶּן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל טָעוּן מְשִׁיחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and moves from the miracles to the rules of who gets anointed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן גדול who is the son of a כהן גדול must be anointed. A king who is the son of a king is not anointed.

steps.title: Then why was שלמה anointed?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא challenges its own rule: שלמה was a king's son, yet he was anointed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: why did they anoint שלמה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a challenge to the rule it just taught. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמה was the son of King דוד, so by the rule he should not have been anointed. Yet the פסוקים tell us he was anointed. That looks like a contradiction to 'we do not anoint a king who is the son of a king.'

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible challenge)

phrases.english: And if you will say:
For what reason did they anoint Solomon?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵם תֹּאמַר: מִפְּנֵי מָה מָשְׁחוּ אֶת שְׁלֹמֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from step 4 using the case of שלמה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a king who is the son of a king is not anointed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלמה was a king's son, yet he was anointed. That seems to go against the rule.

steps.title: Kings' sons were anointed only when someone challenged their right to the throne
steps.stepSummary: שלמה was anointed because of אדוניה's dispute, יהואש because of עתליה, and יהואחז because of his older brother יהויקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the dispute with אדוניה. And יהואש was anointed because of עתליה. And יהואחז was anointed because of his brother יהויקים, who was two years older than him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge. A king's son was anointed only when someone else was fighting him for the throne, and it gives three examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule still stands; these are exceptions. When there is a dispute over who should be king, anointing settles the question publicly. אדוניה tried to take the throne instead of שלמה, and עתליה seized power before יהואש. יהויקים was older, so normally he would have inherited, which is why יהואחז needed anointing.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute, here a fight over the throne

steps.whatToRemember: A king's son is normally not anointed. He is anointed only when there is a dispute over the throne, as with שלמה, יהואש and יהואחז.

phrases.english: Because of the dispute of Adonijah;
and Joash, because of Athaliah;
and Jehoahaz, because of Jehoiakim his brother,
who was older than his brother by two years.
phrases.notes: Since יהויקים was older, he would normally have been next in line. That is why there was a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מַחְלוֹקֶת אֲדוֹנִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 and explains why the cases of שלמה and others do not break the rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception: anointing a king's son is done only when there is a dispute over the throne.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The anointing of שלמה seems to contradict the rule that a king's son is not anointed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule stands. A king's son is anointed only when there is a challenge to his kingship, as with אדוניה, עתליה and יהויקים.

steps.title: Source for anointing a High Priest's son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that even a כהן גדול who is the son of a כהן גדול needs anointing, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said that even a כהן גדול whose father was a כהן גדול must be anointed. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line of the ברייתא from step 4 and asks for its source. This sets up the next step, where a פסוק is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that a son who takes his father's place as כהן גדול simply inherits the job. The ברייתא says he still needs anointing, so the גמרא wants a source that proves it.

keyTerms.meaning: Requires anointing with the special oil
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This is quoting the ברייתא we saw back in step 4.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בֵּן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: And even a High Priest who is the son of a High Priest
requires anointing.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: וַאֲפִילּוּ כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בֵּן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל טָעוּן מְשִׁיחָה. מְנָלַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's rule from step 4 to look for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that a כהן גדול's son also needs anointing.

steps.title: The word 'anointed' shows a son must be anointed
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק adds the word 'המשיח', which teaches that even a son becomes כהן גדול only through anointing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'the anointed priest in his place from among his sons.' It could have just said 'the priest in his place from among his sons.' The extra word 'anointed' teaches that even a son is כהן גדול only if he was anointed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק and points to a word in it that looks extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already says the new כהן is 'from among his sons', so the word 'anointed' seems unnecessary. The גמרא learns from it that being the son is not enough: without anointing, he is not כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the פסוק say (it could have said less)
This is what it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן גדול is made by anointing, not by inheritance, even when he is the son of a כהן גדול.

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And the anointed priest in his place from among his sons"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:15

phrases.english: Let the verse say
"And the priest who is in his place from among his sons"
What does "anointed" add?
This teaches us
that even from among his sons,
the one who was anointed is the High Priest,
and if he was not anointed,
he is not the High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְהַכֹּהֵן הַמָּשִׁיחַ תַּחְתָּיו מִבָּנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'המשיח' in ויקרא 6:15 teaches that even a son needs anointing to become כהן גדול.

steps.title: Source for not anointing a king's son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that a king who is the son of a king is not anointed, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said we do not anoint a king who is the son of a king. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the ברייתא and asks for its source. This sets up רב אחא בר יעקב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule is the opposite of the כהן גדול rule we just saw. So the גמרא needs a separate source showing why kings work differently.

keyTerms.meaning: A king who is the son of a king

phrases.english: The Master said:
We do not anoint a king who is the son of a king.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: אֵין מוֹשְׁחִין מֶלֶךְ בֶּן מֶלֶךְ. מְנָלַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כהן גדול rule to the king rule from the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that a king's son does not need anointing.

steps.title: Kingship is an inheritance
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב shows from a פסוק that kingship passes to the king's sons as an inheritance, so no anointing is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: the פסוק says 'so that he may have long days in his kingdom, he and his sons, all the days.' This shows that the kingdom is an inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers the question with a פסוק about the king's sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the kingdom belongs to the king 'and his sons.' So the son receives it automatically, the same way one inherits property, and he does not need anointing to make him king.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the כהן גדול rule. A כהן גדול's son still needs anointing, but a king's son does not, because kingship is called an inheritance.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
As it is written:
"So that he may have long days in his kingdom,
phrases.notes: דברים 17:20

phrases.english: he and his sons, all the days"
It is an inheritance.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב, דִּכְתִיב: לְמַעַן יַאֲרִיךְ יָמִים עַל מַמְלַכְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'הוא ובניו' in דברים 17:20 show that kingship is an inheritance.

steps.title: Why does a dispute require anointing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats that שלמה was anointed because of אדוניה's dispute, and asks how we know that a dispute requires anointing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they anoint שלמה? Because of the fight with אדוניה. But where do we learn that when there is a fight the new king needs anointing, and that the king cannot simply pass the kingdom to whichever son he wants?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the answer from step 6 about שלמה and asks for its source. This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If kingship is an inheritance, the king might be able to hand it to any son he chooses, even during a fight. The גמרא wants a source showing that a dispute changes the rule and anointing becomes necessary.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute or fight, here over who will be king

phrases.english: And why did they anoint שלמה?
Because of the dispute of אדוניה.
From where do we know that when a dispute arises
anointing is needed,
and that it is not so that whoever the king wants
he can pass the kingship to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה מָשְׁחוּ אֶת שְׁלֹמֹה? מִפְּנֵי מַחְלוֹקֶת אֲדוֹנִיָּה. מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the dispute exception from step 6, now that step 10 showed kingship is an inheritance.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a dispute cancels automatic inheritance and requires anointing.

steps.title: Inheritance works only in peaceful times
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא learns from 'בקרב ישראל' that kingship passes by inheritance only when there is peace in ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the פסוק says 'in the midst of ישראל.' This means at a time when there is peace in ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers from the end of the same פסוק that taught that kingship is an inheritance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inheritance in the פסוק is tied to 'בקרב ישראל', which רב פפא reads as a time of peace. When there is a fight over the throne, the automatic inheritance does not apply, so the new king must be anointed.
steps.whatToRemember: A king's son inherits the throne without anointing only in peaceful times. If there is a dispute, he must be anointed.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The verse says: "In the midst of Israel"
phrases.notes: These are the last words of the same פסוק, דברים 17:20.

phrases.english: at a time when there is peace in Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, אָמַר קְרָא: בְּקֶרֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בקרב ישראל' limits inheritance to a time of peace, so a dispute requires anointing.

steps.title: יהוא was anointed because of a dispute
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that יהוא בן נמשי was anointed only because of the dispute with יורם בן אחאב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: יהוא בן נמשי was also anointed only because of the fight with יורם בן אחאב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that adds יהוא to the list of kings anointed because of a dispute. This sets up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts יהוא in the same group as שלמה: he was anointed because of a fight over the throne, here against the ruling king יורם.

phrases.english: It was taught:

phrases.aramaic: אַף יֵהוּא בֶּן נִמְשִׁי לֹא נִמְשַׁח
phrases.english: Also יהוא son of נמשי was not anointed

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִפְּנֵי מַחְלוֹקֶת יוֹרָם בֶּן אַחְאָב:
phrases.english: except because of the dispute with יורם son of אחאב.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אַף יֵהוּא בֶּן נִמְשִׁי לֹא נִמְשַׁח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another example of anointing because of a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהוא was anointed because of the dispute with יורם בן אחאב.

steps.title: יהוא was a first king anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a dispute is needed as the reason, since יהוא was the first king of his family and would need anointing anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why give that reason? Just say he was anointed because he was a first king!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's reason for anointing יהוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that only a king's son skips anointing. יהוא was not a king's son, he started a new line, so he should need anointing no matter what. Mentioning the dispute seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him get it from (a simpler reason)
A first king, the first of his family to rule

phrases.english: Why?
Let him derive it from the fact that he is a first king!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? תִּיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּמֶלֶךְ רִאשׁוֹן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that יהוא was anointed because of the dispute.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A first king always needs anointing, so the dispute reason is unnecessary.

steps.title: Only kings of בית דוד are anointed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is missing words: kings of בית דוד are anointed but kings of ישראל are not, and יהוא was an exception because of the dispute with יורם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is missing some words, and this is what it means: kings from בית דוד are anointed, but kings of ישראל are not. And if you ask why יהוא was anointed, the answer is because of the fight with יורם בן אחאב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by filling in words that are missing from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since kings of ישראל are normally not anointed at all, being a first king would not be a reason to anoint יהוא. Only the dispute with יורם explains why he was anointed, so the ברייתא's reason is needed after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Something is missing, and this is what it teaches
Kings from דוד's family (the kingdom of יהודה)
Kings of the northern kingdom of ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: Anointing is only for kings of בית דוד. A king of ישראל like יהוא was anointed only because of a special reason, the dispute with יורם.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'ישראל' does not mean the whole Jewish people. It means the northern kingdom, as opposed to בית דוד.

phrases.english: Something is missing, and this is what it teaches:
The kings of the house of David are anointed,
the kings of Israel are not anointed.
And if you say:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה מָשְׁחוּ יֵהוּא בֶּן נִמְשִׁי?
phrases.english: Why did they anoint יהוא son of נמשי?
Because of the dispute with יורם son of אחאב.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 by filling in missing words in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the ברייתא (חסורי מיחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every first king needs anointing, so the dispute reason for יהוא seems unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Kings of ישראל are never anointed, so יהוא needed a special reason: the dispute with יורם.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that anointing is tied to the line of דוד, and that a king outside it is anointed only in an unusual situation.

steps.title: Where do we learn that only kings of בית דוד are anointed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the ברייתא that kings of בית דוד are anointed and kings of ישראל are not, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: the kings of בית דוד are anointed, and the kings of ישראל are not. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from the ברייתא (the corrected wording from step 15) and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 added the rule that only kings from בית דוד get anointed. Now the גמרא wants to know where in the פסוקים this rule comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: Kings from the family of David (the kingdom of יהודה)
Kings of the northern kingdom, who did not come from David's family
From where do we know this?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: מַלְכֵי בֵּית דָּוִד מוֹשְׁחִין,
phrases.english: The Master said: The kings of the house of David are anointed,
phrases.notes: This is the line the גמרא added to the ברייתא back in step 15.

phrases.english: but the kings of Israel are not anointed.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מַלְכֵי בֵּית דָּוִד מוֹשְׁחִין, וְאֵין מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מוֹשְׁחִין. מְנָלַן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule added in the corrected ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that kings of בית דוד are anointed and kings of ישראל are not

steps.title: The פסוק about דוד: this one needs anointing
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'Arise, anoint him, for this is he' teaches that only this line, דוד's family, needs anointing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says, 'Arise, anoint him, for this is he.' This one needs anointing, and no other needs anointing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק said about דוד. The word 'this' (זה) tells us that only דוד's line needs anointing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זה limits the rule. It points to דוד and his family. So kings from other families, like the kings of ישראל, do not need to be anointed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is he': the word זה limits the rule to David

phrases.english: As it is written: "Arise, anoint him, for this is he"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 16:12

phrases.english: this one requires anointing,
and no other requires anointing.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״קוּם מְשָׁחֵהוּ כִּי זֶה הוּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source the previous step asked for
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word זה in the פסוק about David limits anointing to David's line

steps.title: Would we misuse the holy anointing oil just because of a fight with יורם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the holy שמן המשחה could be used on יהוא, a king of ישראל who does not need anointing, just because of a fight with יורם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: because of the dispute with יורם. But just because of a dispute with יורם בן אחאב, would we misuse the holy anointing oil?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line that יהוא was anointed because of the fight with יורם, and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that kings of ישראל do not need anointing. So using the holy שמן המשחה on יהוא would be using holy oil when it is not needed, which is מעילה. A political fight does not seem like enough reason for that.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute or rivalry over who should be king
The holy anointing oil made by משה

phrases.english: The Master said: Because of the dispute with Yoram.
phrases.notes: This goes back to the line in step 13 about why יהוא was anointed.

phrases.english: But because of a dispute with Yoram son of Ahab
shall we misuse the anointing oil?
phrases.notes: He means: use the holy oil for something it isn't needed for, since kings of ישראל don't need anointing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשּׁוּם מַחְלוֹקֶת יוֹרָם בֶּן אַחְאָב נִמְעַל בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule just proven (kings of ישראל are not anointed) to attack the case of יהוא
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that יהוא was anointed because of the dispute with יורם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A king of ישראל does not need the holy oil, so using it on him would be misusing holy property

steps.title: He was anointed with pure balsam, not the holy oil
steps.stepSummary: Following רב פפא, יהוא was anointed with pure balsam oil, so no holy oil was misused.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב פפא said: with pure balsam. Here too, it was with pure balsam.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by using a statement of רב פפא: the anointing was done with pure balsam, not with the holy שמן המשחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed יהוא was anointed with the holy oil. The answer is that a different, ordinary oil was used. That shows he was king in a public way, and no holy oil was used up.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure balsam oil, an ordinary (not holy) fine oil
Here too: the same idea applies in this case

phrases.english: As Rav Pappa said: With pure balsam,
phrases.notes: רב פפא said this about יהואחז, who comes up in the next line of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: here too, it was with pure balsam.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בַּאֲפַרְסְמָא דַּכְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by changing which oil was used
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: a different oil was used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יהוא was anointed with the holy שמן המשחה
steps.terutzMaskana: יהוא was anointed with pure balsam, so there was no misuse of holy oil

steps.title: יהואחז was anointed because of יהויקים, who was two years older
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: יהואחז was anointed because of יהויקים, who was two years older than him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And יהואחז was anointed because of יהויקים, who was two years older than him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next line of the ברייתא so it can examine it. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a son who follows his father as king of בית דוד does not need a new anointing. Here יהואחז was anointed because his older brother יהויקים could claim the throne. The anointing made it clear who the king was.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of יאשיהו who became king after him
Another son of יאשיהו, a rival for the throne

phrases.english: And Yehoachaz was anointed because of Yehoyakim,
who was two years older than him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶת יְהוֹאָחָז מִפְּנֵי יְהוֹיָקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יהואחז needed anointing because his older brother יהויקים was a rival for the throne

steps.title: But the פסוק calls יוחנן, who is יהואחז, the firstborn
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק lists יוחנן as the firstborn and יהויקים as second, and רבי יוחנן says יוחנן is יהואחז. So יהויקים was not older.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was יהויקים really older? The פסוק says: 'The sons of יאשיהו: the firstborn יוחנן, the second יהויקים, the third צדקיהו, the fourth שלום.' And רבי יוחנן said: יוחנן is יהואחז, and צדקיהו is שלום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's claim that יהויקים was older, using a פסוק plus רבי יוחנן's explanation of the names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts יוחנן first and יהויקים second. If יוחנן is the same person as יהואחז, then יהואחז was the oldest. Then there was no older brother to fight with, and no reason to anoint him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He is ... he is': two names for the same person

phrases.english: And was he older?
But isn't it written: "And the sons of Josiah: the firstborn Yochanan,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 3:15

phrases.english: the second Yehoyakim, the third Tzidkiyahu,
the fourth Shallum,"
and Rabbi Yochanan said: He (Yochanan) is Yehoachaz,
and he who is Tzidkiyahu is Shallum!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי קַשִּׁישׁ? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the fact given in the previous step
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that יהויקים was two years older than יהואחז
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls יוחנן (who is יהואחז) the firstborn, so יהואחז was the oldest

steps.title: יהויקים really was older; יהואחז was first to reign
steps.stepSummary: יהויקים really was older. יהואחז is called 'firstborn' because he was the first to become king.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, יהויקים really was older. Why does the פסוק call יהואחז 'firstborn'? Because he was first in kingship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the ברייתא's fact and explains the פסוק in a new way. 'Firstborn' here means first to rule, not first to be born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge read בכור as birth order. The answer reads it as the order of reigning. That way the פסוק and the ברייתא no longer contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually: keeps the original claim
First in kingship: the first of the brothers to reign

phrases.english: Rather, Yehoyakim really was older,
and why does it call him (Yochanan) firstborn?
Because he was firstborn to the kingship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם יְהוֹיָקִים קַשִּׁישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by reading the word בכור differently
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בכור in the פסוק means first born, which would make יהואחז the oldest
steps.terutzMaskana: בכור means first to reign, so יהויקים can still be older

steps.title: Do we crown a younger son before an older one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the younger brother could be made king, since the פסוק says יהושפט gave the kingdom to יהורם because he was the firstborn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we put the younger son ahead of the older one? But the פסוק says: 'And he gave the kingdom to יהורם, because he was the firstborn'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. If יהויקים was older, why was the younger יהואחז made king first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of יהורם shows that the kingdom goes to the firstborn. So making the younger son king first seems to break that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The younger one ahead of the older one

phrases.english: And do we appoint the younger before the older?
But isn't it written: "And he gave the kingdom to Yehoram,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 21:3. The 'he' is יהושפט, יהורם's father.

phrases.english: because he was the firstborn"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מוֹקְמִינַן זוּטָא קַמֵּי קַשִּׁישָׁא? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer that the younger יהואחז reigned first
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the younger יהואחז was made king before the older יהויקים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק about יהורם shows that the kingdom goes to the firstborn

steps.title: יהורם was worthy to fill his fathers' place
steps.stepSummary: יהורם got the kingdom because he was firstborn and also worthy to fill his fathers' place. An older son who is not worthy can be passed over.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one (יהורם) was fit to fill the place of his fathers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the firstborn gets the throne only if he is fit to fill his fathers' place, as יהורם was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being firstborn matters only when the son is also worthy. יהורם was worthy, so being firstborn won him the kingdom. יהויקים was not considered worthy, so the younger יהואחז could be crowned first, and that is why he needed anointing.

keyTerms.meaning: Fills the place of his fathers: worthy to take over his father's role

steps.whatToRemember: Only kings of בית דוד are anointed, learned from 'כי זה הוא'. יהוא was anointed with pure balsam, not the holy oil. יהואחז was anointed because his older brother יהויקים was a rival. The firstborn gets the throne only if he is worthy of his fathers' place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that kingship goes to the firstborn only when he is worthy. Being born first is not enough by itself.

phrases.english: That one was filling the place of his fathers.
phrases.notes: He means יהורם was worthy to rule. Being worthy, not just being older, is what counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא מְמַלֵּא מְקוֹם אֲבוֹתָיו הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by setting a limit on the firstborn rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making a distinction: worthy firstborn versus unworthy firstborn
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The firstborn always gets the kingdom
steps.terutzMaskana: The firstborn gets the kingdom only if he is worthy, as יהורם was; יהויקים was not

steps.title: Quoting the line: שלום is צדקיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוחנן's statement from step 21: שלום and צדקיה are the same person.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: שלום is צדקיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי יוחנן's statement, quoted in step 21, that שלום and צדקיה are the same person. It is setting up a question about this statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that two names, שלום and צדקיה, belong to one king. The גמרא quotes him now so it can test this against the order of the פסוק in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A name that appears in the list of יאשיהו's sons
The last king from בית דוד before the destruction

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: הוּא שַׁלּוּם הוּא צִדְקִיָּה.
phrases.english: The Master said: Shallum is Zedekiah.
phrases.notes: This is quoting what רבי יוחנן said back in step 21.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the discussion of יהואחז and יהויקים, the גמרא returns to the other half of רבי יוחנן's statement from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלום and צדקיה are one person.

steps.title: But the פסוק counts them one after another
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק lists צדקיה as third and שלום as fourth, so it seems they are two different people.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the פסוק counts them in a row!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's statement. The פסוק that lists יאשיהו's sons counts צדקיה and שלום as two separate sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק says 'the third, צדקיהו; the fourth, שלום', it sounds like two people. That seems to clash with רבי יוחנן's claim that they are one person.

keyTerms.meaning: In a row, one after another, in order

phrases.english: But it counts them in a row!
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק in דברי הימים א 3:15, which lists the sons as first, second, third and fourth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בְּדָרֵי קָחָשֵׁיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the line quoted in step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that שלום is צדקיה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists a 'third' son and a 'fourth' son with different names, which sounds like two people.

steps.title: Third by birth, fourth to be king
steps.stepSummary: צדקיה is called 'third' because he was third born, and 'fourth' (as שלום) because he was the fourth to rule, after יהואחז, יהויקים and יכניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is he called 'third'? Because he was third among the sons. Why is he called 'fourth'? Because he was fourth to the kingdom, since יכניה ruled before him. First יהואחז ruled, then יהויקים, then יכניה, then צדקיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק counts the same person twice, in two different ways. Once by birth order and once by order of becoming king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Third' is his place among the brothers by birth. 'Fourth' is his place in the line of kings. יכניה ruled between יהויקים and צדקיה, so צדקיה was the fourth king even though he was only the third son.

keyTerms.meaning: Fourth to the kingdom (in the order of kings)
A king who ruled between יהויקים and צדקיה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'third' and 'fourth' are two different people. It is one person counted two ways: by birth and by when he became king.

phrases.english: And why does it call him third?
Because he is third of the sons,
And why does it call him fourth?
phrases.notes: Here 'fourth' is the name שלום in the פסוק, which רבי יוחנן says is צדקיה.

phrases.english: Because he is fourth to the kingship,
because Jeconiah reigned before him –
first Jehoahaz reigned,
and afterward Jehoiakim reigned,

phrases.aramaic: וְסוֹף מְלַךְ יְכָנְיָה, וְסוֹף מְלַךְ צִדְקִיָּה.
phrases.english: and afterward Jeconiah reigned, and afterward Zedekiah reigned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי קָרֵי לֵיהּ שְׁלִישִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק as counting the same person in two different orders.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list in the פסוק is a simple birth list, so 'third' and 'fourth' must be different people.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Third' means by birth, 'fourth' means by order of ruling; both refer to צדקיה.

steps.title: Why he was called שלום
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives two reasons for the name שלום: he was complete in his deeds, or the kingdom of בית דוד came to its end in his days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: שלום is צדקיה. Why was he called שלום? Because he was complete (שלם) in his deeds. Another explanation: שלום, because the kingdom of בית דוד was completed (ended) in his days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees שלום is צדקיה and explains where the name שלום comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons play on the word שלם, 'complete'. The first is praise: his deeds were complete. The second is about history: the rule of בית דוד was 'completed', meaning it came to an end, in his time.

keyTerms.meaning: The kingdom of the house of דוד

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוּא שַׁלּוּם הוּא צִדְקִיָּה,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Shallum is Zedekiah,
and why was his name called Shallum?
Because he was complete in his deeds.
Another explanation: Shallum –
because the kingdom of the house of David was completed in his days,
phrases.notes: 'Completed' here means it came to an end.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הוּא שַׁלּוּם הוּא צִדְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having shown that שלום is צדקיה, the גמרא brings a ברייתא explaining the name שלום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He was called שלום either because his deeds were complete or because בית דוד's kingdom ended in his days.

steps.title: His real name was מתניה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says his original name was מתניה, and the king of בבל changed it to צדקיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what was his name? מתניה was his name, as it says: 'He made מתניה his uncle king in his place, and changed his name to צדקיה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and tells us his original name, proving it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So this one king has three names: מתניה (his real name), צדקיה (the name the king of בבל gave him) and שלום (a description). The פסוק shows the name change happened when he was made king.

phrases.english: And what was his name? Mattaniah was his name,
as it is stated: "And he made Mattaniah his uncle king in his place,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 24:17. The one doing this is the king of בבל.

phrases.english: and changed his name to Zedekiah,"

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה שְׁמוֹ? מַתַּנְיָה שְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, moving from the name שלום to his real name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His real name was מתניה; the king of בבל renamed him צדקיה.

steps.title: Why the name צדקיה
steps.stepSummary: נבוכדנצר named him צדקיה as a warning: God will justify judgment against you if you rebel against me. And צדקיה did rebel, breaking his oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he said to him: God will justify (יצדיק) the judgment against you if you rebel against me. As it says: 'And he brought him to בבל', and it is written: 'And he also rebelled against King נבוכדנצר of בבל, who had made him swear by God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why the new name was צדקיה. It was a warning connected to the oath צדקיה made not to rebel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name צדקיה comes from צדק, 'justice'. נבוכדנצר was saying: if you rebel, God will be just in punishing you. The פסוקים show he had power to take kings to בבל, and that צדקיה rebelled anyway even though he swore by God.

keyTerms.meaning: Will justify the judgment against you (show your punishment is fair)

steps.whatToRemember: One king, three names: מתניה (real name), צדקיה (a warning name from נבוכדנצר), שלום (complete in deeds, or the end of בית דוד's rule).

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: לוֹ יָהּ יַצְדִּיק עָלֶיךָ אֶת הַדִּין
phrases.english: For he said: God will justify the judgment against you
phrases.notes: 'He' is נבוכדנצר, speaking to צדקיה. The name צדקיה sounds like 'יה will justify'.

phrases.english: if you rebel against me,
as it is stated: "And he brought him to Babylon,"
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 36:10.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב: ״וְגַם בַּמֶּלֶךְ נְבוּכַד נֶאצַּר מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל מָרָד
phrases.english: and it is written: "And he also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 36:13.

phrases.english: who had made him swear by God."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר: לוֹ יָהּ יַצְדִּיק עָלֶיךָ אֶת הַדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the name change mentioned in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The name צדקיה was a warning that God would justly punish him if he broke his oath and rebelled.

steps.title: Was there still anointing oil in יהואחז's time?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how יהואחז could be anointed, since a ברייתא says the שמן המשחה was hidden away together with the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: And was there anointing oil? But it was taught: from when the ארון was hidden away, the jar of מן was hidden away, and the flask of anointing oil, and אהרן's staff with its almonds and flowers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's claim that יהואחז was anointed and challenges it. It brings a ברייתא that the anointing oil had been hidden away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anointing a king needs the special שמן המשחה. But a ברייתא lists the anointing oil among the holy items hidden together with the ארון. If it was hidden before יהואחז's time, how could he be anointed with it? The ברייתא continues in the next step, and רב פפא answers in step 34.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy anointing oil made by משה
Was hidden away (stored out of use)
The jar of מן kept as a reminder

phrases.english: And was there anointing oil?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the earlier line that יהואחז was anointed.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: from when the Ark was hidden away,
the jar of manna was hidden away,
phrases.notes: See שמות 16:33.

phrases.english: and the flask of anointing oil,
and Aaron's staff with its almonds and blossoms,
phrases.notes: See במדבר 17:23.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי הֲוָה שֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of צדקיה's names and returns to the ברייתא's statement that יהואחז was anointed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement in step 20 that יהואחז was anointed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Anointing requires שמן המשחה, but a ברייתא says it was hidden away along with the ארון, so it seemingly was not available.

steps.title: The Philistine gift chest, and יאשיה hid it all
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the chest of gold gifts sent by the פלשתים was also hidden with the ארון, and יאשיה מלך יהודה was the one who hid everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also hidden was the chest the פלשתים sent as a gift to the God of ישראל, as the פסוק says: 'Put the gold vessels you return to Him as an אשם in a chest at its side.' Who hid it? יאשיה, king of יהודה, as the פסוק says: 'The king said to the כהנים: Put the holy ארון...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the same ברייתא it brought in step 31. It adds one more hidden item and names the king who hid everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chest was kept 'at the side' of the ארון, so it was hidden along with the ארון. Naming יאשיה matters for our question, because יהואחז ruled after יאשיה. That means the oil was already hidden when יהואחז was anointed, so the question from step 31 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A chest or box. Here it means the box of gold items the פלשתים sent back with the ארון.
A guilt offering. The gold items were sent as a payment for having taken the ארון.
He hid it away, stored it out of sight

phrases.english: And the chest that the Philistines sent
as a gift to the God of Israel,
as it is stated: "And the vessels of gold
that you return to Him as a guilt offering,
you shall put in the chest at its side."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 6:8

phrases.english: And who hid it away?
Josiah, king of Judah, hid it away,
as it is stated: "And the king said to the priests:
Put the holy Ark"
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 35:3. The פסוק goes on: 'in the house that שלמה built.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַרְגַּז שֶׁשִּׁגְּרוּ פְּלִשְׁתִּים דּוֹרוֹן לֵאלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted as the basis of the challenge in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פלשתים' gift chest was hidden with the ארון, and יאשיה hid everything.

steps.title: Three word-links tie the items to the ארון
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains why these items were hidden with the ארון: three גזירה שוה links connect the ארון, the מן, the שמן המשחה and the staff of אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It is learned from 'there' and 'there,' from 'generations' and 'generations,' and from 'to be kept' and 'to be kept.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the source for why the oil and the other items were kept next to the ארון. Because they were kept there, they were hidden with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'there' links the ארון to the jar of מן. The word 'generations' links the מן to the שמן המשחה. The word 'to be kept' links the מן to the staff of אהרן. Like a chain, all of them end up beside the ארון, so the oil was really hidden with it, and the question about יהואחז gets stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from, it is learned from. This signals a גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה.
Learning a law from the same word appearing in two places in the תורה
The jar of מן kept as a reminder for future generations
אהרן's staff that blossomed, kept as a sign
Something to be kept or guarded

steps.confusionAlert: The links are a chain. Not every item is linked straight to the ארון: the oil and the staff are each linked to the מן, and the מן is linked to the ארון.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
It is learned from "there" and "there,"
phrases.notes: This links the ארון (שמות 30:6) with the jar of מן (שמות 16:33).

phrases.english: it is learned from "generations" and "generations,"
phrases.notes: This links the מן (שמות 16:33) with the anointing oil (שמות 30:31).

phrases.english: it is learned from "to be kept" and "to be kept."
phrases.notes: This links the מן with אהרן's staff (במדבר 17:25).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אָתְיָא ״שָׁם״ ״שָׁם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source from the פסוקים for why the items listed in the ברייתא were kept, and hidden, with the ארון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through three גזירה שוה links, the מן, the שמן המשחה and אהרן's staff all belong beside the ארון.

steps.title: יהואחז was anointed with pure balsam
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers the question from step 31: יהואחז was not anointed with the hidden שמן המשחה, but with pure balsam oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: With pure balsam.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question of how יהואחז could be anointed if the special oil was already hidden. He says a different oil was used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that 'anointing' a king had to mean the שמן המשחה. רב פפא says the anointing of יהואחז was done with pure balsam instead. This way the ברייתא about hiding the oil and the report that יהואחז was anointed no longer clash.
steps.whatToRemember: The שמן המשחה was hidden by יאשיה together with the ארון. When יהואחז was later anointed, it was done with pure balsam, not the holy oil.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
With pure balsam.
phrases.notes: He means יהואחז was anointed with balsam, not with the real anointing oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בַּאֲפַרְסְמָא דַּכְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 31, which steps 32 and 33 made stronger.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the anointing used a different oil.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The anointing of יהואחז must have used the שמן המשחה, which was already hidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: יהואחז was anointed with pure balsam, so the hidden oil was not needed.

steps.title: Kings are anointed like a crown, priests like a 'chi'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the shape of the anointing: a crown shape for kings and a 'chi' shape for כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: kings are anointed in the shape of a crown, and priests in the shape of a 'chi'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that describes the shape of the oil when kings and כהנים were anointed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps discussed whether certain kings were anointed and with which oil. Now the גמרא turns to how the anointing was physically done. A king gets a ring of oil around the head like a crown, and a כהן gets a different shape called 'chi'.

keyTerms.meaning: in the shape of, something like

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One anoints the kings in the shape of a crown,
and the priests in the shape of a "chi."
phrases.notes: "Priests" here means the כהן גדול, who was anointed with this oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מוֹשְׁחִין אֶת הַמְּלָכִים כְּמִין נֵזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which oil kings were anointed with to the shape of the anointing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kings are anointed in a crown shape; כהנים in a 'chi' shape.

steps.title: רב מנשיה explains: a Greek 'chi'
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיה explains that the 'chi' shape means the Greek letter chi, which looks like an X.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיה said: it means like the Greek letter 'chi'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשיה clarifies the strange word 'כי' in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think 'כי' means the Hebrew letters כ and י. רב מנשיה says it is the Greek letter chi, shaped like an X. So the oil was placed on the כהן's head in a crossing shape.

keyTerms.meaning: the Greek letter chi, shaped like an X

phrases.english: Rav Menashya said:
Like a Greek "chi."
phrases.notes: The Greek letter chi looks like an X, so the oil made an X shape.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָה: כְּמִין כִּי יְוָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word in the ברייתא of step 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'chi' shape is the Greek letter X.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about the order of pouring and anointing
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says first pour oil on the head, then place oil between the eyelashes; another ברייתא says the opposite.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: first he pours oil on his head, and afterward places oil between his eyelashes. Another ברייתא teaches: first he places oil between his eyelashes, and afterward pours oil on his head!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two ברייתות contradict each other about which comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Anointing the כהן גדול has two parts: pouring oil on the head and placing oil between the eyelashes. The two ברייתות give opposite orders. The גמרא needs to explain this contradiction.

phrases.english: One ברייתא teaches:
First he pours oil on his head

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ נוֹתֵן לוֹ שֶׁמֶן בֵּין רִיסֵי עֵינָיו,
phrases.english: and afterward he places oil between his eyelashes,
and another ברייתא teaches:

phrases.aramaic: בַּתְּחִלָּה נוֹתֵן לוֹ שֶׁמֶן בֵּין רִיסֵי עֵינָיו
phrases.english: First he places oil between his eyelashes

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַצִּיק לוֹ שֶׁמֶן עַל רֹאשׁוֹ!
phrases.english: and afterward he pours oil on his head!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues describing how the anointing is done, and raises a contradiction about the order.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the two parts of anointing the כהן גדול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות give opposite orders for pouring and anointing.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים about which act is more important
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two ברייתות reflect two תנאים: one holds anointing is more important, the other holds pouring is more important.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute of תנאים: one holds anointing is preferable, and one holds pouring is preferable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by saying each ברייתא follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The more important act comes first. One תנא thinks anointing between the eyelashes is more important, so it comes first. The other thinks pouring on the head is more important, so it comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: it is a dispute between תנאים
anointing (smearing oil, here between the eyelashes)

phrases.english: It is a dispute of תנאים,
there is one who says anointing is preferable,
and there is one who says pouring is preferable.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 37.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each ברייתא to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do not contradict; they follow two תנאים who disagree about which act is more important.

steps.title: Why is pouring more important?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason of the תנא who says pouring is preferable.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the one who says pouring is preferable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking for the source of the opinion that pouring comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After saying there are two opinions, the גמרא wants to know what each side is based on. It starts with the pouring side.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר יְצִיקָה עֲדִיפָא –
phrases.english: What is the reason of the one who says pouring is preferable?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר יְצִיקָה עֲדִיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of one side of the dispute in step 38.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the view that pouring is preferable

steps.title: The פסוק says pouring came first
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק says משה poured the oil on אהרן's head, and only afterward mentions anointing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And he poured of the anointing oil on אהרן's head.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that lists pouring first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'ויצק' (he poured) and then 'וימשח' (he anointed). Since pouring comes first in the פסוק, this תנא holds it is the more important act.

phrases.english: As it is said:
"And he poured of the anointing oil on Aharon's head,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 8:12

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיִּצֹק מִשֶּׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה עַל רֹאשׁ אַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק mentions pouring first, so pouring is preferable.

steps.title: Why anointing is more important: it was also done to the כלי שרת
steps.stepSummary: The other תנא holds anointing is more important because anointing was used more widely, also on the כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says anointing is preferable holds this because anointing was also included for the service vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for the other side: anointing is more important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כלי שרת of the משכן were anointed, but the פסוקים never say oil was poured on them. Since anointing is used in more places, this תנא sees it as the main act.

keyTerms.meaning: the service vessels of the משכן

phrases.english: And the one who says anointing is preferable,

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבָּה אֵצֶל כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת.
phrases.english: holds: because it was included for the service vessels.
phrases.notes: The vessels were anointed with this oil, but oil was never poured on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר מְשִׁיחָה עֲדִיפָא קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the second side of the dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Anointing is preferable because it was also done to the כלי שרת.

steps.title: But the פסוק says pouring came first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the anointing side: the פסוק clearly says 'he poured' and only afterward 'he anointed'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written 'he poured' and only afterward 'he anointed'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the view that anointing comes first, using the order of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If anointing is more important and should come first, how does this תנא explain the פסוק? It lists pouring before anointing, which seems to support the other side.

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"And he poured," and only afterward "and he anointed"!
phrases.notes: Both words are from the same פסוק, ויקרא 8:12.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב: וַיִּצֹק וּלְבַסּוֹף וַיִּמְשַׁח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion given in step 41.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that anointing is preferable and comes first
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists pouring before anointing.

steps.title: The pouring happened because he had already been anointed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the פסוק differently: the pouring was done because of the anointing that made him holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: what is the reason for 'he poured'? Because 'he anointed him to sanctify him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the פסוק in a new way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of words in the פסוק is not the order of the actions. 'He anointed him to sanctify him' explains why the pouring could happen. So anointing is the main act and came first.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
What is the reason for "he poured"?
Because "he anointed him to sanctify him."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: מָה טַעַם וַיִּצֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 42.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק shows pouring came first.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק means pouring happened because of the anointing, which came first.
steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות about the order follow two תנאים. One says pouring is more important, based on the order of the פסוק. The other says anointing is more important, because it was also done to the כלי שרת, and reads the פסוק to fit this view.

steps.title: Two pearl-like drops hung from אהרן's beard
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the פסוק in תהלים: two drops of oil like pearls hung from אהרן's beard.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'Like the good oil running down on the head, etc.' Two drops like pearls were hanging from אהרן's beard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that describes what happened to the oil after אהרן was anointed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in תהלים describes the oil running down onto אהרן's beard. The ברייתא says two drops of oil stayed hanging there, looking like pearls.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"Like the good oil running down on the head, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 133:2

phrases.english: Something like two drops, like pearls,
were hanging on Aharon's beard.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כַּשֶּׁמֶן הַטּוֹב הַיּוֹרֵד עַל הָרֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the order of anointing to what happened to the oil on אהרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two pearl-like drops of oil hung from אהרן's beard.

steps.title: The drops rose to the roots of his beard when he spoke
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא brings a teaching that when אהרן spoke, the drops would rise and settle at the roots of his beard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said, it was taught: when he would speak, they would rise and settle at the roots of his beard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא adds a detail to the story of the drops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When אהרן spoke, his beard moved, and you would expect the drops to fall. Instead they miraculously rose up and stayed at the roots of his beard.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said, it was taught:
When he would speak,
phrases.notes: Here מספר means talking, not cutting hair.

phrases.english: they would rise and settle at the roots of his beard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, תָּנָא: כְּשֶׁהוּא מְסַפֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to the drops described in step 44.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When אהרן spoke, the drops rose to the roots of his beard instead of falling.

steps.title: משה רבינו worried he had misused the holy oil
steps.stepSummary: משה רבינו worried that the extra drops meant he had used too much oil and misused the holy שמן המשחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about this matter משה our teacher worried: perhaps, God forbid, I misused the anointing oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by telling us that משה רבינו was worried because of these drops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holy oil may not be used for anything other than its holy purpose. משה feared that the leftover drops meant he had poured too much, which would be מעילה, misusing something holy.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה הָיָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ דּוֹאֵג,
phrases.english: And about this matter Moshe our teacher was worried,
perhaps, God forbid,
I misused the anointing oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל דָּבָר זֶה הָיָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ דּוֹאֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells משה's reaction to the drops from steps 44 and 45.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה worried that the extra drops showed he had misused the שמן המשחה.
steps.whatToRemember: Two pearl-like drops of שמן המשחה stayed on אהרן's beard. They did not fall even when he spoke, and משה רבינו worried they meant he had misused the holy oil.

steps.title: A heavenly voice says the oil on the beard is like dew
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול answers משה's worry: just as dew has no מעילה, the oil running down אהרן's beard has no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said: 'Like the dew of Hermon that comes down on the mountains of Zion.' Just as dew cannot be misused as holy property, so too the oil that runs down on אהרן's beard cannot be misused.
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven answers משה's worry from the last step. The oil on אהרן's beard does not count as misusing holy property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה was afraid the extra drops showed he had used too much holy oil. The בת קול uses the next words of the same מזמור in תהלים, which compare the oil to dew. Dew belongs to everyone and is not holy, so in the same way the oil on the beard carries no מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Misusing holy (הקדש) property for personal benefit

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said:
"Like the dew of Hermon that comes down on the mountains of Zion"
phrases.notes: תהלים 133:3. It is the same מזמור that speaks about the oil on אהרן's beard.

phrases.english: Just as dew cannot be misused as holy property,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שֶׁמֶן שֶׁיּוֹרֵד עַל זְקַן אַהֲרֹן
phrases.english: so too the oil that runs down on אהרן's beard
cannot be misused as holy property.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry משה raised in step 46.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The oil on the beard is like dew, so it has no מעילה.

steps.title: אהרן still worries that he himself misused the oil
steps.stepSummary: Even after the answer to משה, אהרן worries that משה may be cleared but he himself may have misused the oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still אהרן was worried: maybe משה did not misuse the holy oil, but I did!
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with a new worry, this time from אהרן. This step sets up the next heavenly answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer cleared משה, who poured the oil. אהרן was the one with the oil on him, so he feared he was the one getting benefit from holy property.

phrases.english: And still אהרן was worried:
maybe משה did not misuse the holy oil,
but I did misuse it!
phrases.notes: The oil was sitting on אהרן's own body, so he was afraid he was the one benefiting from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲדַיִין אַהֲרֹן הָיָה דּוֹאֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a second worry that the answer to משה did not fully settle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אהרן feared that he, and not משה, had committed מעילה.

steps.title: A heavenly voice tells אהרן that he is clear like his brother
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול quotes 'how good and pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together': just as משה did not misuse the oil, neither did אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said to him: 'Behold how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell together.' Just as משה did not misuse the holy oil, you did not misuse it either.
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven answers אהרן's worry. The two brothers are treated the same, so neither of them committed מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the answer comes from the first פסוק of the same מזמור, which speaks about brothers being together. The brothers are linked, so the ruling that cleared משה also clears אהרן. This closes the story about the drops of oil.
steps.whatToRemember: The two drops of oil on אהרן's beard were not מעילה. The בת קול cleared משה (the oil is like dew) and then cleared אהרן (brothers are treated alike).

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said to him:
"Behold how good and how pleasant
phrases.notes: תהלים 133:1

phrases.english: it is for brothers to dwell together"
Just as משה did not misuse the holy oil,
so too you did not misuse it.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצְתָה בַּת קוֹל וְאָמְרָה לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אהרן's worry from step 48 and closes the story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Like his brother משה, אהרן did not commit מעילה.

steps.title: Kings are anointed only beside a spring
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that kings are anointed by a spring so that their kingship will continue, based on שלמה being anointed at גיחון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: We anoint kings only beside a spring, so that their kingship will continue. As it says: 'And the king said to בניהו... and bring him down to גיחון... and anoint him there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic connected to anointing: where kings are anointed. A ברייתא gives the rule, the reason, and the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A spring keeps flowing, so anointing a king beside one is a good sign that his kingship will keep going too. The proof is that דוד המלך ordered שלמה to be anointed at גיחון, which was a spring.

keyTerms.meaning: So that their kingship will continue
Gihon, the spring where שלמה was anointed

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
We do not anoint kings
except beside a spring,
so that their kingship will continue,
as it says: "And the king said to Benaiah, etc.
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:33–34. The king is דוד, giving orders for שלמה to be anointed.

phrases.english: and bring him down to Gihon, etc.
phrases.notes: גיחון is a spring, and that is the whole proof.

phrases.english: and anoint him there."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מוֹשְׁחִין אֶת הַמְּלָכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the anointing of the כהן גדול to the anointing of kings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kings are anointed only beside a spring, as a sign that their kingship will continue.

steps.title: A lamp as a sign for whether one will live through the year
steps.stepSummary: רב אמי teaches that someone who wants to know whether he will live through the year can hang a lamp in a windless house during the ten days between ראש השנה and יום כיפור. If it keeps burning, he will finish his year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אמי said: Someone who wants to know whether he will live through the year should bring a lamp during the ten days between ראש השנה and יום כיפור and hang it in a house where no wind blows. If its light keeps going, he will know that he will finish his year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a side teaching about good signs, like the sign of the spring for kings. רב אמי describes a lamp test for the coming year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The connection is the idea of 'continuing'. The spring flows on, and here the lamp's light keeps going. A windless house is used so that only a lamp that truly goes out by itself counts as a sign.

keyTerms.meaning: The year continues (he will live through the year)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new halacha about lamps or ראש השנה. It is a side teaching about signs, brought in because it shares the 'continuing' idea of the spring for kings.

phrases.english: רב אמי said:
Someone who wants to know
whether the year will continue for him or not
phrases.notes: He means whether he will live through this year.

phrases.english: should bring a lamp
during these ten days
that are between Rosh HaShana and Yom Kippur,
and hang it in a house where no wind blows.
If its light keeps going,
he will know that he will finish his year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַמֵּי: הַאי מַאן דְּבָעֵי לִידַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching about good signs, like the spring used for anointing kings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lamp that keeps burning in a windless house during the ten days between ראש השנה and יום כיפור is a sign that one will live through the year.

steps.title: The rooster sign for business success
steps.stepSummary: Someone who wants to know if his business will succeed should raise a rooster. If it grows fat and handsome, the business will succeed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And someone who wants to go into business and wants to know whether it will succeed should raise a rooster. If the rooster gets fat and handsome, he can know his business will succeed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second sign to רב אמי's list. This one is about whether a business will succeed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lamp sign in step 51 was about life. This sign is about money. The pattern is the same: if the thing you set up does well (the lamp keeps burning, the rooster thrives), it is a good sign for you.

phrases.english: And one who wants to do business
and wants to know
whether his business will succeed or not
should raise a rooster.
If it gets fat and handsome,
phrases.notes: "It" is the rooster, not the business.

phrases.english: he will know that he will succeed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּבָעֵי נַעֲבֵיד עִיסְקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second sign to רב אמי's list, after the lamp sign for living through the year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a rooster raised for this purpose grows fat and handsome, the business will succeed.

steps.title: The dark-house sign for returning from a journey begins
steps.stepSummary: Someone who wants to know if he will come home safely from a trip should go into a dark house. If he sees... (the sentence continues on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who wants to set out on a journey and wants to know whether he will come back home should go in and stand in a dark house. If he sees...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a third sign, about whether a traveler will come home. The sentence stops in the middle, so the rest of this sign comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sign follows the same shape: a person who wants to know X does a set action, and the result tells him the answer. Here the action is standing in a dark house. What he needs to see is told on the next amud.

phrases.english: This one who wants to go out on a journey
and wants to know whether he will return to his home
should go in and stand in a dark house.
If he sees

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאן דְּבָעֵי נִיפּוֹק בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third sign to the same list, this time about travel. It continues past the end of this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A traveler who wants to know if he will return should stand in a dark house and check whether he sees something (finished on the next amud).
